name: Fairmont Mayakoba
positioning: Resort in the Mayakoba community, designed around a network of waterways, with ocean-view suites, five pools and an on-site golf course
best_for: Families, since children eat free from the children's menu and have free Kids Club programming
Golfers who want the El Camaleón course on site
Travelers who want a butler-style Balam host and exclusive activities

facts.text: Fairmont Mayakoba was the first resort built in the Mayakoba community, where construction began in 2003.
Accommodations are split between rooms, casitas and suites, with views of the mangroves, the canal or the Caribbean Sea depending on category.
Rooms reflect modern Mexican design and have deep marble soaking tubs.
The resort has five swimming pools, three of them along the oceanfront.
Dining includes the Greek restaurant Gaia and Ki, a beach bar and Korean grill.
El Camaleón is a Greg Norman-designed 18-hole championship golf course.
The Dive & Water Sports Center offers scuba diving, jet ski rentals and private yacht charters.
Most spa treatments draw inspiration from Mayan cosmology and are based on the lunar calendar.
Valet parking is included in all stays (one car per room) and the resort has no self-park lots.
Cancun International Airport is about 30 miles (48 kilometers) from the resort.

highlights.text: Certain bookings include access to a Balam, a special assistant similar to a butler, and a select itinerary of exclusive activities.
The spa garden has a grounding path lined with Melipona beehives, a cold plunge pool and a temazcal sweat lodge.
Children eat free when choosing from the children's menu and have free programming at the Balam and Coatí Kids Clubs.
The Beach Front Suite has a private terrace with an infinity pool and ocean views.

considerations.text: The all-inclusive package does not include El Pueblito or the El Camaleón Golf Course.
Pets are not allowed in the pool or beach areas.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires transportation planning.
